topic: Where do we put all the excess carbon dioxide?

primary_direction.name: PERSIST-CO2
primary_direction.expanded_name: Permanence, Energy, Reversal, Storage Integrity, and Trade-offs for CO2
primary_direction.claim: A permanence-aware portfolio can reduce worst-case climate-benefit regret while meeting lifecycle, resource, monitoring, equity, and stewardship constraints better than single-pathway or nominal-cost strategies.
primary_direction.research_object: A staged pathway portfolio and monitoring program evaluated in a scenario ensemble.
primary_direction.falsification: Reject PERSIST-CO2 if it does not outperform single-pathway and nominal-cost policies on held-out durability-adjusted regret under equal accounting and physical constraints, or if its advantage requires perfect monitoring or unbounded resources.

candidate_routes.name: geology-first
candidate_routes.strength: High durability potential and concentrated storage target
candidate_routes.weakness: Site integrity, infrastructure, pressure, monitoring, and stewardship constraints

candidate_routes.name: biology-first
candidate_routes.weakness: Reversal, additionality, land, water, and permanence risks

candidate_routes.name: engineered-removal-first
candidate_routes.strength: Can target atmospheric CO2 and some durable pathways
candidate_routes.weakness: Energy, cost, material, ecological, and scale constraints

candidate_routes.name: avoidance-only
candidate_routes.weakness: Does not address residual emissions or legacy atmospheric CO2

candidate_routes.name: PERSIST-CO2
candidate_routes.strength: Couples durability, lifecycle, resources, monitoring, equity, and stewardship
candidate_routes.weakness: Requires integrated data, model calibration, and long-term governance

predictions: MRV capacity can bind before physical storage capacity.
Staged deployment and liability triggers outperform delayed or unbounded scale-up.
